html:
SMTO-PSM-0018 — The connection form and the raw value were both changed

GUID: 7e1a1c32-1be1-4f8e-b58d-f275304913ab
Slug: parameter-value-conflict
Domain: PSM · Subsystem: psm

What happened

  • You changed a web connection parameter in two ways at once, through its form and through its raw saved value. SMTO didn't save either change, so your stored sign-in details are untouched.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Reload the Parameter Store page and open the parameter again. This clears the half-made changes so you start from what is actually saved.
  2. To change normal settings such as the address, use only the connection form on the Value tab, then select Save. The form updates the fields you change and keeps your saved passwords and tokens.
  3. Only if you need to replace the whole saved value, open Advanced: reveal and replace raw saved value, edit there, and don't touch the form. SMTO accepts one kind of change per save, so it never has to guess which one you meant.

What success looks like

  • Parameter Store shows Saved and the parameter shows your change.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't paste hidden values (shown as dots) back into the value box; that would replace your real password.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A Parameter Store editor save supplied both public_http_profile (structured HTTP connection fields) and value_json, so editor_payload rejected the ambiguous replacement.

What this means

  • The parameter editor receives both a structured public HTTP configuration and raw value_json for the same edit. Accepted parameter bindings preserve exact identity and revision. Validation does not authorize secret substitution, alias guessing or replay of earlier work; failed write confirmation requires reading the original stored state.

Why this can happen

  • The parameter editor receives both a structured public HTTP configuration and raw value_json for the same edit.

How to diagnose it

  • Identify the intended editing mode and preserve private credentials behind public projections.

How to fix it

  • Send either public_http_profile or value_json in one create/update request, not both (editor_payload in src/agent_runtime/api/agent_ui_support/route_groups/parameters.py). Never write a masked (••••) projection back as value_json; that would overwrite stored credentials.
  • Choose the supported structured HTTP editor or a raw parameter value for this edit. Do not overwrite a stored credential with a redacted projection.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • One supported representation updates the intended fields without overwriting hidden credentials.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • Accepted parameter bindings preserve exact identity and revision. Validation does not authorize secret substitution, alias guessing or replay of earlier work; failed write confirmation requires reading the original stored state.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
